headline: Controversial audio clip: Cantonment Police OC withdrawn
summary: Md Rakibul Hasan was removed from his post after a recording allegedly showing him criticizing the government and police force went viral.
details: The officer-in-charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, Md Rakibul Hasan, has been withdrawn and attached to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) headquarters.
The decision follows the circulation of an audio clip on social media in which he allegedly made controversial remarks about the government, administration, and police.
In the recording, a voice allegedly belonging to the OC is heard criticizing the government, the Bangladesh Army, and the police force, claiming that police on the streets are 'very weak'.
The clip also contains allegations that senior police officials were leaning towards the BNP, while personnel on the ground were not.
Furthermore, the speaker in the audio clip describes alleged bribery within the police force and claims that police postings are secured through bribes.
DMP officials stated that the contents of the audio clip will be examined, and appropriate action will be taken against the OC if necessary.
Md Rakibul Hasan has claimed that the viral audio clip was created using AI, denying the remarks.
caption:
A police chief removed after a viral audio clip allegedly criticizing the government and exposing bribery in the force.

The officer-in-charge (OC) of Cantonment Police Station, Md Rakibul Hasan, has been withdrawn and attached to the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) headquarters.

The decision follows the circulation of an audio clip on social media in which he allegedly made controversial remarks about the government, administration, and police.

In the recording, a voice allegedly belonging to the OC is heard criticizing the government, the Bangladesh Army, and the police force, claiming that police on the streets are 'very weak'.

The clip also contains allegations that senior police officials were leaning towards the BNP, while personnel on the ground were not.

Furthermore, the speaker in the audio clip describes alleged bribery within the police force and claims that police postings are secured through bribes.

DMP officials stated that the contents of the audio clip will be examined, and appropriate action will be taken against the OC if necessary.

Md Rakibul Hasan has claimed that the viral audio clip was created using AI, denying the remarks.

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star

headline: ACC seeks financial details of Asif Mahmud and wife
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission is investigating allegations of money laundering and illicit wealth acquisition by the former interim government adviser.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has requested the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) for comprehensive details of bank accounts, assets, and overseas investments of former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and his wife.

The ACC is investigating allegations that Asif Mahmud acquired illicit wealth while serving as an adviser, laundered money abroad, and established offshore shell companies in Portugal, Australia, Dubai, Singapore, and Switzerland.
The commission is seeking information on all bank accounts, credit cards, safety deposit lockers, bonds, and loans held by the couple, including active, dormant, and closed accounts.
Specific allegations include the laundering of Tk 11,000 crore to five different countries, with the largest sums allegedly sent to Dubai (Tk 4,500 crore) and Singapore (Tk 3,000 crore).

Further claims suggest Tk 60 crore was exchanged for the appointment of an administrator to Dhaka North City Corporation and commissions were taken from development projects in various city corporations.
The ACC has also initiated inquiries into alleged irregularities in recruitments, transfers, and procurements at the Ministry of Youth and Sports during his tenure.
When disclosing wealth statements on February 11, 2026, Asif Mahmud reported assets worth Tk 15.3 lakh, noting he did not have a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) before joining the cabinet.
caption:
Tk 11,000 crore money laundering allegations. The ACC is now digging into the financial records of former adviser Asif Mahmud.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has requested the Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit (BFIU) for comprehensive details of bank accounts, assets, and overseas investments of former interim government adviser Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and his wife.

The commission is seeking information on all bank accounts, credit cards, safety deposit lockers, bonds, and loans held by the couple, including active, dormant, and closed accounts.

Specific allegations include the laundering of Tk 11,000 crore to five different countries, with the largest sums allegedly sent to Dubai (Tk 4,500 crore) and Singapore (Tk 3,000 crore).

Further claims suggest Tk 60 crore was exchanged for the appointment of an administrator to Dhaka North City Corporation and commissions were taken from development projects in various city corporations.

The ACC has also initiated inquiries into alleged irregularities in recruitments, transfers, and procurements at the Ministry of Youth and Sports during his tenure.

When disclosing wealth statements on February 11, 2026, Asif Mahmud reported assets worth Tk 15.3 lakh, noting he did not have a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) before joining the cabinet.
